ASSIGNMENT #4 · GUIDED PRACTICE

Build, Deploy & Test a Binary Classification Model

A step-by-step Azure Machine Learning Designer project: predict whether annual income is ≤ $50K or > $50K using the Adult Census Income dataset.

Supervised learningTwo-class logistic regressionAzure ML DesignerReal-time endpoint

1. Understand the project

Imagine a system that receives information about a person—such as age, education, occupation and weekly working hours—and predicts one of two income categories. You will create that system using a labeled dataset: each training record includes an income category, so the algorithm can learn relationships between the input features and the known answer.

Input (features)

Age, education, occupation, hours per week and other selected columns.

Target (label)

income: ≤50K or >50K.

Prediction

The trained model estimates an income category for a new record.

The prediction is a statistical estimate, not a verified statement about an individual. This exercise uses sensitive demographic attributes from a historical dataset; discuss potential bias and do not use this demonstration for consequential decisions.

2. What you will accomplish

  1. Prepare the Adult Census Income dataset for modeling.
  2. Train and evaluate a binary classification model using a 70/30 train–test split.
  3. Turn the trained model into a real-time inference pipeline.
  4. Deploy the model to an endpoint and send a JSON request using curl.
  5. Capture a screenshot showing the returned income prediction.

3. Follow the project in four phases

01

Prepare the data · Original steps 1–3

Open Azure ML Designer, add the built-in Adult Census Income dataset, select meaningful columns, remove rows with missing values and split the dataset: 70% training / 30% testing.

02

Train and evaluate · Original steps 4–8

Add Two-Class Logistic Regression, train with income as the label, connect the test data to Score Model, evaluate the results and run the pipeline on a compute instance. Review the evaluation metrics before deployment.

03

Deploy for predictions · Original steps 9–15

Configure the Kubernetes deployment target described below, create a Real-Time Inference Pipeline, confirm Web Service Input/Output, submit it, deploy, and wait until the endpoint is ready. Copy your own endpoint URL and primary key.

04

Test and submit · Original steps 16–18

Create payload.json using the sample record below. Send it to your deployed endpoint with curl. Confirm the response includes a predicted income label and take a screenshot of the command prompt.

4. Before you begin

  • Access to an Azure Machine Learning workspace and Designer, with permissions to run jobs and deploy endpoints.
  • Available compute resources and sufficient Azure quota; deployment can incur cloud charges.
  • A command-line terminal with curl and a text editor for payload.json.

Income Prediction (≤50K or >50K)

Objective

You will build a complete machine learning pipeline using Azure Machine Learning Designer to predict whether an individual’s income is:

  • ≤ 50K

  • > 50K

This is a binary classification problem using supervised learning.

Dataset

Use the built-in dataset:

  • Adult Census Income Dataset

This dataset contains demographic and employment-related information such as:

  • age

  • education

  • occupation

  • hours per week

  • marital status

  • income (target label)

Build Complete ML Pipeline

17. Run the following 'curl' command in command line to request and receive output from the model via endpoint:

curl -X POST "YOUR_ENDPOINT_URL" ^
-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIMARY_KEY" ^
-H "Content-type: application/json" ^
-d "@C:\dev\payload.json"

NOTE:

  • Endpoint: YOUR_ENDPOINT_URL

  • Primary Key as Authentication
